citations.assessment: Huna reports the teaching on the new heavens and earth in his name.
Huna reports the teaching about the person who completes an act receiving credit. Yochanan’s neighboring statement is distinctly attributed.
Zakut expressly attributes the thirty-two measures to Eliezer son of Yose the Galilean. This is textual attribution, with the baraita’s printed history still open.
Yochanan quotes Elazar son of Shimon as the one recommending attention to the aggadah of Eliezer son of Yose. Keep the two names distinct.
Reciprocal Heilprin entry explicitly states the brotherhood and cites a court chronology. Yuchasin also states this relationship.
The reciprocal entry specifies the Yerushalmi reference; the transmitted words are also recoverable in that passage.
The bare names are consecutive in one chain. The reciprocal Heilprin entry points to this passage.
Near the end of the paragraph Yochanan expressly cites Eliezer son of Yose the Galilean in an a fortiori argument about separation.
Huna in his name explains the generations effaced before revelation. Text variants differ over the count; Heilprin does not quote a number here.
Huna expressly gives the Noah account in the name of Eliezer son of Yose.
The reciprocal entry records this burial for the son, then gives other reports for the father. Its travel-source witnesses remain provisionally identified.
Chapter 39 contains another exact report by Huna in this sage’s name. It is a plausible reading of the corrupt numeral, pending printed collation.
